entries.title: Chat can build on your earlier conversations
entries.body: When you type a question in Chat, the AI is given a short list of your other Chat conversations about the same article. If one of them already took up the same question, it is asked to open that conversation and build on it. The one-line descriptions in that list are kept for the AI and never shown to you.

entries.title: The back button returns only your place
entries.body: After you jump to another passage, from a link, the strip showing where you are, or a search result, the '↩ back to …' button takes you back to where you were and changes nothing else. Before, it also reopened or closed modes to match the moment of the jump, much like the browser's Back.

entries.title: Reporting a failed import includes its details
entries.body: When an import fails, Report this fills the Feedback box with the article's address, or the name of the file you uploaded, and the error, so you do not have to copy them in. We also keep a record of each import, removed when you delete the article, and the privacy policy says so.

entries.title: Text sizes match from one mode to another
entries.body: Titles, quotations, explanations, counts and labels had drifted to slightly different sizes in each mode. Many of them now share one set of sizes across Skim, Timeline, FAQ, Glossary, Ideas, Quotes, Citations, Debate, Referee and Search, so the same kind of line looks the same wherever you meet it.

entries.title: The Feedback box is larger on big screens
entries.body: On a large window the Feedback box is wider, and taller too where the window has the height for it, so what you write has more room.

entries.title: Back button no longer covers Chat's typing box
entries.body: On a phone, when a mode's panel covers the article, the '↩ back to …' button sat over the panel's last row, which in Chat was the start of the box you type into. The panel now leaves room for it. Nothing changes when the panel sits beside the article.
